vip.name: Nancy Pelosi
vip.why: The original "follow her trades" name for retail investors, with a multi-year record of beating the market. Trades are few but large and concentrated, typically tech and AI-adjacent names, often via call options.
vip.watch: Most filings are made for her husband Paul Pelosi and listed under her name. Big option positions are the signal to watch.

vip.name: Tommy Tuberville
vip.why: Repeatedly ranked among Congress's most profitable and market-beating traders in Capitol Trades-style year-end reviews.
vip.watch: Senate filings, often in batches. Amended reports can surface trades that are months old, marked "amended" here.

vip.name: Josh Gottheimer
vip.why: One of the most active House traders that also scores well on volume-weighted return rankings, so the activity comes with results rather than noise.
vip.watch: Frequent small trades. Larger bands ($100K+) carry more signal.

vip.name: Tim Moore
vip.why: Quiver Quantitative ranked his disclosed portfolio the best-performing in Congress for 2025 (reported by the NY Post), at roughly +52%.
vip.watch: Few but sizeable trades, so each new filing is worth reading.

vip.name: Ted Cruz
vip.why: Quiver's 2025 ranking put him second in Congress at roughly +50%.
vip.watch: Trades rarely, so any new disclosure stands out.

vip.name: Lisa McClain
vip.why: Ranked in Quiver's 2025 top tier at roughly +37% while trading actively across sectors.
vip.watch: Files frequently. Watchlist overlaps (e.g. MSFT) show up here first.

vip.name: Cleo Fields
vip.why: Ranks highly in 2026 Capitol Markets-style tables for dollar outperformance against the S&P 500 (SPY).
vip.watch: Mostly mega-cap tech buys in the $1K–$15K band, so the direction matters more than the size.

vip.name: Michael McCaul
vip.why: Discloses large technology trades and is closely followed, partly because of committee-related conflict-of-interest debates.
vip.watch: Large household and trust positions. Filings can be paper scans with longer lags.

vip.name: Mitch McConnell
vip.watch: Mostly spouse accounts and dividend reinvestments. Discretionary buys and sells are the signal.

vip.name: Markwayne Mullin
vip.why: Historically cited for large winning trades, e.g. Nvidia before the AI rally. Kept on the list for continuity.
vip.watch: No longer a sitting senator. His last filing was March 2026, so expect no new disclosures; a candidate for the next quarterly review.

vip_criteria.summary: VIPs are picked for track record and signal quality, not trade count: members whose disclosed portfolios have beaten the market, or whose concentrated trades are widely followed.
rules: Ranked near the top of public Congress performance leaderboards (Quiver Quantitative, Capitol Trades, Capitol Markets) for the latest full year.
Concentrated positions or large size bands, where one trade means something.
Excluded: high-volume "spray" traders (e.g. Ro Khanna, Gilbert Cisneros) who report hundreds of tickers and often lag the index. Their filings still appear here if they hit the Watchlist.
Reviewed quarterly against the leaderboards. Returns are estimates from the statutory size bands, not exact P&L.
